newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Curacao refinery sees higher ouput in 17 days.
newsitem.headline: Curacao refinery sees higher ouput in 17 days.

text.p: The fire-striken Curacao oil refinery, operated by Venezuela's state-run Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), will raise throughput by 10,000 bpd to 115,000 bpd in 17 days, a senior official at the refinery said Monday.
The 310,000 bpd capacity refinery was hit by a serious fire on Thursday last week. Initially, the official had expected to reach 120,000 bpd within one to two weeks.
But weekend inspections revealed that it would take until Aug 21-25 before throughput can rise.
And a full repair would take a couple of months, he added.

"We think we could take the atmospheric tower into operation in 17 days, but the vacuum tower will take a couple of months to repair. If we can restart (the atmospheric tower) it will take us to 115,000 bpd, only 15,000 bpd below normal use of that unit," he said.

Thursday's fire disabled the largest crude distillation unit at the refinery, cutting throughput by 130,000 bpd to 60,000 bpd. The plant was now running 60,000 bpd through its number two crude unit and 45,000 bpd in a thermal cracking unit that was converted into a crude distiller.
Crude unit number two had been scheduled to go into a four- week maintenance in August, and the official said this was now expected to happen once the damaged crude distiller has been restarted.
He said the refinery expected to import 15,000 tonnes of naphtha for gasoline production and two 13,000-tonne cargoes of aviation fuel to fulfill its contractual requirements this month.

As well as the usual refined product output, the refinery processes 50,000 bpd of Lagomar crude to make lubricants. This crude is now being processed in PDVSA's Cardon refinery and the long residue was due to be delivered to Curacao for its lube oil train.
